deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of the Paris prize essay on heat conduction (1861), the 'Commentatio mathematica' published posthumously in Werke 1876. Pars secunda asks when a quadratic differential form sum b_{ii'} ds_i ds_{i'} can be transformed into sum dx_i^2. Equivalently, since a positive form with constant coefficients reduces to a sum of squares, the question is when it can be transformed into a form with constant coefficients. On the previous page: (3) b_{ii'} = sum_nu x_{nu,i} x_{nu,i'} and (4) sum_nu (ds_i/dx_nu)(ds_{i'}/dx_nu) = beta_{ii'}/B, which is the inverse metric. Here x_{nu,i} = dx_nu/ds_i. (5) defines p_{i,i',i''} = 2 sum_nu x_{nu,i} x_{nu,i'i''} = d_{i''} b_{ii'} + d_{i'} b_{ii''} - d_i b_{i'i''}. In modern terms p is twice the Christoffel symbol of the first kind, 2Gamma_{i,i'i''}.

Step (6): 2 d^2x_nu/ds_{i'}ds_{i''} = sum_i (ds_i/dx_nu) p_{i,i',i''}. [My filling] Substitute p, sum over i, and use sum_i (ds_i/dx_nu)(dx_mu/ds_i) = delta_{nu mu}. Modern form: x_{nu,i'i''} = sum_i (ds_i/dx_nu) Gamma_{i,i'i''}.

Step 2: differentiate p again and antisymmetrise in (i'', i'''). The third-derivative terms 2 sum x_{nu,i} x_{nu,i'i''i'''} cancel. My computation gives d_{i'''} p_{i,i',i''} - d_{i''} p_{i,i',i'''} = 2 sum_nu (x_{nu,ii'''} x_{nu,i'i''} - x_{nu,ii''} x_{nu,i'i'''}).

Step 3: substitute (6) and (4). [Mine] This gives sum_nu x_{nu,ab} x_{nu,cd} = (1/4) sum_{k,k'} p_{k,a,b} p_{k',c,d} beta_{kk'}/B. Expanding p in terms of b gives (I): 2(d^2 b_{ii''}/ds_{i'}ds_{i'''} + d^2 b_{i'i'''}/ds_i ds_{i''} - d^2 b_{ii'''}/ds_{i'}ds_{i''} - d^2 b_{i'i''}/ds_i ds_{i'''}) + (1/2) sum_{k,k'} (p_{k,i,i'''} p_{k',i',i''} - p_{k,i,i''} p_{k',i',i'''}) beta_{kk'}/B = 0. The page leaves blanks for the last two second-derivative terms and for the quadratic p-term; the margin note asks to leave space. The left side, denoted (ii', i''i'''), is (up to a factor of -4 or so and sign conventions) the covariant Riemann curvature tensor R_{i i' i'' i'''}. Its vanishing is a necessary condition for local flatness.

Step 4: to show the meaning of the symbols, form E = dd(sum b ds ds) - 2 d delta(sum b ds delta s) + dd(sum b delta s delta s). This is a second variation of the metric along two directions d and delta. The second-order variations d^2, d delta, delta^2 are fixed by a condition that is left blank on the page. [My reading] The condition makes the first-variation terms vanish for arbitrary delta', i.e. geodesic/normal-coordinate type conditions. Result (II): E = sum (ii', i''i''') (ds_i delta s_{i'} - ds_{i'} delta s_i)(ds_{i''} delta s_{i'''} - ds_{i'''} delta s_{i''}), summed over pairs i < i' and i'' < i''' (margin). This is the curvature tensor as a quadratic form in the bivector d wedge delta, i.e. R(d, delta, d, delta).

Step 5: E is defined invariantly, so under a change of variables it transforms into the corresponding expression for the new form. If the b are constant, all coefficients vanish. Hence a form transformable to constant coefficients must have II identically zero.

Step 6: (III) = (1/2) E / (|d|^2 |delta|^2 - <d,delta>^2), with a sign change per the margin note 'mit -1 multiplicirt'. It is invariant under change of variables and, as the next page says, under replacing (d, delta) by independent linear combinations. This is the sectional (Riemannian) curvature K(d wedge delta). The next page interprets it as the Gaussian curvature of the geodesic surface spanned by d and delta.
errors: As transcribed, the right side of the differentiated-p identity is 2 sum x_{ii''} x_{i'i'''} - 2 sum x_{ii'''} x_{i'i''}. Direct computation gives the opposite sign: 2 sum x_{ii'''} x_{i'i''} - 2 sum x_{ii''} x_{i'i'''}. The handwriting of the indices is ambiguous, so this may be a reading problem; otherwise it is a sign slip. Such a slip would be absorbed in the overall sign of (I), and the margin 'mit -1 multiplicirt' suggests sign adjustments were made.

Formula (I) is incomplete on this sheet. Two of the four second-derivative terms and the whole quadratic term in p and beta/B are left blank (margin: leave space). The defining condition for the second-order variations after 'ita, ut sit' is also blank. These are lacunae of this copy, not mathematical errors.
The numerator of (III) is written as shorthand '1/2 Sigma (ii', i''i''')'. The bivector factors of (II) are understood.

There Riemann's curvature symbol (ii', i''i''') and the sectional-curvature quotient are famous and already credited to him. The only novelty is manuscript-level detail: blanks, margin notes and sign adjustments.

transcription_corrections: Formula (I): the first term should read d^2 b_{i,i''}/ds_{i'} ds_{i'''}, not ds_{i'} ds_{i''}. The manuscript most likely has i''' in the denominator.
Margin note at (I): read 'N.B. 2 Zeilen lassen' ('leave two lines'), not '2 vorg. [?] lassen'. It refers to the blank left in formula (I) and/or after 'ita, ut sit'.
After 'ita, ut sit' there is a genuine blank in the manuscript (the defining formula involving delta' is missing). This is not a transcription omission.
'cifrae [-ae-]aequales': the manuscript has 'cifrae aequales' with a struck-through false start before 'aequales'.
